steps.what: Establish the required replacement tire or tube specification and quantity
Find matching supplier items and compare availability and price
Check suitability and order replacements from the selected supplier

tasks.design: Use approved saved searches and order templates in {PARTNER_PORTAL}, optionally linked to {PROCUREMENT}. Match exact size and rating fields deterministically, then have the technician verify suitability and approve the final supplier order.
tasks.previous_blocker: Specifications are repeatedly typed into supplier searches and order forms.
tasks.enabler_now: Native catalogue filters and saved order lines can reuse verified requirements.
tasks.still_hard: A dimension match alone does not establish load, speed, construction or vehicle compatibility.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise an unsuitable replacement and seek clarification before ordering.
tasks.altitude: Less catalogue searching and order entry; replacement selection and spending authority remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Supplier identifiers, compatibility limits and order terms

evidence.claim: Exact specification filters and saved supplier order lines can reduce repeated search and entry; tire-ordering compatibility and savings are E1 model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is establishing the replacement requirement and placing its order, excluding tire removal, fitting, supplier fulfilment and stock receipt.

The tire technician produces vehicle or job ID, tire size, construction, load and speed rating, tube type where relevant, quantity and needed date in s1. All 40 hours remain for reading markings, checking requirements and capturing fields. Unknown or inconsistent markings require manual clarification.

The supplier's existing catalogue supplies SKU, specification, price and availability. The technician checks currency and compatibility within 14 retained s2 hours and 15 retained s3 hours; missing matches or substitutions require manual selection, never an inferred fit.
Test native supplier filters and saved orders before custom integration. Any new approved-reference maintenance by the parts coordinator is counted below; no free compatibility database is assumed.
unknowns: Supplier catalogue coverage and native saved-order features
Technician spending authority and approved substitutions
research_questions: Can a trial reduce search and entry while preserving every specification and suitability check?

already_counted.description: Requirement capture, catalogue exceptions and final order verification

incremental.description: Maintain saved searches and handle catalogue changes
Maintain approved replacement references and supplier mappings

approvals.approved_version: Exact supplier, SKU, specification, quantity, price, delivery date and destination; any change requires renewed order approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=40+14+15=69; gross 31%, minus four focal upkeep gives 27% central net. Low assumes nine search and entry hours removable because many specifications need manual matching; all physical requirement checks remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Spend less time re-entering tire requirements while retaining replacement suitability and order approval.
reach: Maintain reliable replacement references with the parts coordinator
role.ambitious_version: A tire technician who can obtain the correct replacement with fewer repeated searches.
